- [x] **T-168** 'Run the full suite alone' must become a check: assert peer idleness before the run and refuse or flag when a peer is busy (session 173) — Opened session 77 on Aaron's ruling. THE RULE NAMES A CONDITION NO SEAT COULD VERIFY. 'Run the full suite alone at every candidate' has been in briefs since Loop 16 and every seat believed it was following it; the QA seat's slice-three baseline was run 'alone' while the planner was demonstrably active mid-run (a rulings message arrived during it) and the developer was working G-045, and it went red. A seat that believes it ran alone has an instrument that cannot tell 'nothing else was running' from 'I did not look' - G-044's class, in the one rule meant to guard the measurement. PROJECT DOCTRINE SETTLES THE FIX: a rule someone has to remember is an intention; a check is a rule. THE CHECK IS NOW POSSIBLE AND WAS DONE BY HAND TONIGHT: ListAgents lists every peer session on the machine with a busy/idle state, and calling it immediately before the suite is what made V-076's measurement mean anything. Without it the clean idle run would have been one more unlabelled data point in a table of eleven. SHAPE: before a full-suite run at a candidate, the seat calls ListAgents; if any peer is busy it REFUSES or flags loudly in the report, and either way the peer states at run time are recorded ALONGSIDE the result so a later reader can tell a contended run from a clean one. Every historical sighting lacks that field, which is why eleven measurements cannot be re-read. LIMITS TO BUILD IN, from this session's own findings: ListAgents has a REGISTRATION LAG - the developer's listing showed only the planner while the QA seat was already running - so an early or short listing is indistinguishable from a machine with nothing on it, and the check must not read an empty listing as 'idle' without a control (D-029 records this). It also cannot see non-Claude load (a build, a browser, an indexer), so it is a necessary and not a sufficient condition and must be worded as such rather than as a guarantee of idleness. RELATED: G-042 (the fault this protects the measurement of), V-076 (the controlled comparison), T-166 (another instrument that reported confidence it had not earned). --- AMENDED session 78, and Aaron ruled the policy (D-034): THE PEER SET IS NO LONGER ONLY SIA'S SEATS. On 2026-09-23 around 02:14Z the A2A-Hub planner seat (worktrees-82, a different project on the same machine) was BUSY during the developer's full suite on candidate A's working tree. Run 1 exited 1 with G-042's signature (1096 passed, 2 skipped, 1 unhandled onTaskUpdate timeout). Run 2 was clean after that seat was asked to make no tool calls. The developer and QA seats agree that both surviving hypotheses are LOAD, either external (the other project's seat) or the suite's own (candidate A adds about 153s of spawning at full parallelism), and that neither is separated yet. An interactive seat can also show BUSY while its human types. POLICY (D-034): other projects' seats work normally BY DEFAULT and are RECORDED beside every SIA suite result; they pause only when a SIA seat requests a controlled rerun.
